Q: Change multiple Autosys jobs Status in one go A:

I think that after 7 years you must have found a solution but for others try this:

sendevent -E JOB_ON_ICE -J jobname1

You can check the status before and after with this command:

autorep -j jobname1

This is my first answer on StackOverflow, thanks for your encouragement :)

Q: How to manipulate gpio from the binary running in Docker container? A:

When building the Docker image, also the call to setcap is necessary. Full list of conditions I needed to satisfy, to make it work for me:

  • /dev/port file needs to have r/w permissions, solved it with /etc/udev/rules.d/90-port-chmod.rules: KERNEL=="port", MODE="0777"; note that 777 is probably exaggerated
  • docker compose file needs SYS_RAWIO capability, device mapping is fine
  • the Dockerfile needs to grant raw IO capabilities to the binary in question; also if the binary links to some libraries specified in user env LD_LIBRARY_PATH that would not work anymore, so linker has to be globally configured
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1

FROM oraclelinux:9
RUN useradd --home-dir /home/my_user --uid 1000 --create-home --shell /bin/bash my_user
USER my_user
WORKDIR /home/my_user
RUN mkdir -p /home/my_user/bin
COPY --chown=my_user --chmod=0755 gpio_test /home/my_user/bin/gpio_test
USER root
RUN setcap cap_sys_rawio=ep /home/my_user/bin/gpio_test
RUN echo "/home/my_user/lib/" > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/my_user_libs.conf && ldconfig
USER my_user
ENTRYPOINT ["tail", "-f", "/dev/null"]

Now calling gpio_test binary from within the running container can alter the state of /dev/port controlling the GPIO.
